model.title: Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act
model.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Lloyd Smucker (R-PA)

summary.text: The bill would exclude from federal taxable income certain damages, other than punitive damages, received because of a sexual act or sexual contact, whether or not there are medical records or observable injuries. It would also provide that a court or settlement statement saying damages arise from such an act or contact counts as credible evidence and meets the taxpayer's burden of proof on that point. The changes would apply to payments under decisions made or agreements entered into after the bill's enactment, with rules for when a decision or replacement agreement counts as made after that date. The bill would also state that it does not imply anything about whether physical injury or sickness includes cases without medical records or observable injuries. Finally, the Treasury Secretary, working with the Department of Justice Office on Violence Against Women and other agencies, would run a program to raise public awareness of this exclusion.
